title: Ala Singh’s Expansion and the Decision to Strike Sirhind

blocks.text: The narrative first follows Ala Singh and allied chiefs as their local influence expands, helped by Khalsa protection and the weakening of older authorities. Territory, kin connections, and prestige all widen together, so the page reads as a record of growing power rather than mere survival.

Need soon pushes the Khalsa back toward direct action. The Singhs want resources to travel for the congregation at Amritsar, and they ask Kapoor Singh for permission to strike a wealthy center that can finance both devotion and movement.

Sirhind becomes the chosen target because memory and justice weigh alongside opportunity. Labh Singh reminds the Panth that this is The town where Guru’s two Sahibzadas were executed, so a raid on Sirhind answers practical need while also avenging one of the deepest wounds in Sikh memory.
